section_summary: Most of this section is an enclosure from the March 1941 issue of the Spanish-language magazine Oriente y Occidente, containing articles on Asian culture, Japanese society, literature, wartime aviation, economics, industrial chemistry, books, advertisements, and reader testimonials. It is followed by the conclusion of an Embassy despatch concerning Salvadoran Consul General Leon Siguenza and by U.S. War Department intelligence material. The final memorandum reports an alleged clandestine channel in which messages from South America were concealed in motion-picture film cans shipped to Japan for collection by Japanese military or naval intelligence agents.

subfiles.title: Continuation of an unidentified patriotic essay
subfiles.about: A concluding fragment exhorts readers to honor their spiritual inheritance by faithfully fulfilling their duties.
subfiles.summary: Continuation of a patriotic essay urging the present generation to prove worthy of its predecessors and defend its institutional patrimony.

subfiles.title: Habrá una exposición de maquinarias japonesa
subfiles.about: A Japanese industrial exhibition is announced for South American ports aboard the Montevideo Maru.
subfiles.summary: News brief: Japanese industry groups planned a June machinery exhibition aboard the Montevideo Maru visiting Brazil, Buenos Aires and Montevideo; the machinery was not for sale.

subfiles.title: Supersticiones Chinas en la Ficción y Folklore
subfiles.about: An essay explains Chinese popular beliefs about the soul, karma, ghosts, reincarnation, and revenge through fictional examples.
subfiles.summary: The author presents Chinese superstition as a mixture of Confucian, Taoist, and Buddhist ideas, describing parallel earthly and spiritual bureaucracies, the hun and po souls, judgment by Yama, and karmic rebirth. Several stories illustrate ghosts returning to assist or punish their families, including the tale of Niu Ching-chang. Other examples explain wayward children as creditors reincarnated to recover debts and portray revenge continuing across this life, Hades, and later existences. The essay concludes that such beliefs support social order by promising eventual punishment for wrongdoing.

subfiles.title: Amarú: Poeta de la India
subfiles.about: A selection of short poems attributed to Amaru treats love, jealousy, forgiveness, separation, and emotional surrender.
subfiles.summary: The poems use intimate dialogue and Indian natural imagery such as lotus flowers, rivers, monsoon rains, swans, and rice fields. Their speakers repeatedly try and fail to resist love, with tears or memory overcoming anger and pride. Named figures including Hamita, Sarmitcha, and Critavima appear in the lyrical vignettes.

subfiles.title: Primary Education in Nippon
subfiles.about: A statistical note praises the reach and patriotic orientation of Japanese primary education.
subfiles.summary: Note claims 99.8 percent of Japanese children attend primary school, gives national totals, and describes a new eight-year national-school plan beginning in 1941.

subfiles.title: Odisea de Tierra Firme
subfiles.about: A condensed novel excerpt follows the Riolid family from provincial Venezuela to Pablo Riolid’s political exile and opposition to the Gómez dictatorship.
subfiles.summary: The narrator recounts a family history rooted in Cumbres, beginning with a great-grandfather who married Anita Guillaume after independence and prospered through agriculture and Caribbean trade. Later generations embody the tension between inherited provincial tradition and the desire for adventure. Pablo Riolid joins student opposition to General Gómez, escapes Caracas for Curaçao, and participates in an abortive revolutionary conspiracy centered on Machetazito. An editorial note explains that the novel’s despair reflected the dictatorship and contrasts it with Venezuela’s emerging post-Gómez national confidence.

subfiles.title: El País de Thai
subfiles.about: A short profile describes independent Thailand, Bangkok, its population, transport, dress, temples, foreign communities, and performing arts.
subfiles.summary: Country profile of Thailand's independence and Bangkok's temples, canals and floating commerce; Chinese form the largest foreign colony, followed by Japanese.

subfiles.title: Recuerdos del verano en Japón
subfiles.from: Setsuo Uenoda; translated by Elida Karlen
subfiles.about: An illustrated cultural essay surveys summer heat, fairs, bathing, family life, judo, and holiday travel in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Translated article on a Japanese summer: festivals, shaved ice, Kodokan training, hot baths as purification, family gardens, and youth holidays in the mountains, at beaches or in Korea.

subfiles.title: Kokoro: Kimiko
subfiles.about: A story recounts the rise, self-sacrifice, disappearance, and religious renunciation of the celebrated geisha Kimiko.
subfiles.summary: Born Ai into an impoverished former samurai family, Kimiko sells herself into geisha life so that Kimika can support her mother and educate her sister. She becomes Kyoto’s most admired geisha but refuses permanent attachment until pity leads her to live with a wealthy young admirer. Convinced that her past would disgrace his family, she disappears, enabling him to marry and have a son. Years later she briefly returns as a mendicant Buddhist nun, revealing through a message to the child the depth of her continuing sacrifice.

subfiles.title: Los Gobelinos advertisement
subfiles.from: Los Gobelinos; P. de Miguel Sáez y Cía.
subfiles.about: An advertisement promotes a home-furnishings specialist with branches in Buenos Aires, Rosario, and Paris.
subfiles.summary: Los Gobelinos advertisement for upholstery, linens, carpets and furniture, with Buenos Aires, Rosario and Paris addresses.

subfiles.title: Los Estudiantes del Cielo
subfiles.about: A war correspondent accompanies military weather specialists on a hazardous observation flight.
subfiles.summary: Article on flying with a colonel and young observer to 5,000 meters to record weather with wing-mounted instruments, translated into forecasts for combat pilots.

subfiles.title: Banco Municipal de Préstamos branch notice
subfiles.about: A notice announces a new municipal pawnshop branch in Buenos Aires.
subfiles.summary: Banco Municipal de Prestamos announces Branch No. 7 opening at Corrientes 3099 on March 1, for clothing pledges only.

subfiles.title: Ante la Nueva Economía Mundial
subfiles.about: Giacomo Acerbo evaluates the raw-material requirements and limits of a prospective continental European economy.
subfiles.summary: Acerbo examines Europe's dependence on imports of wheat, cotton, wool and rubber, concluding absolute continental autarky is impossible and intercontinental exchange must continue.

subfiles.title: Nuestro Amigo el Carbón
subfiles.about: A popular-science article surveys the many medical, industrial, military, and consumer products derived from coal tar.
subfiles.summary: Popular-science article presenting coal as the basis of medicines, synthetic gasoline, plastics and explosives, explaining coal-tar distillation and stressing sulfanilamide and sulfapyridine.

subfiles.title: Libros Recibidos
subfiles.about: A review column lists recently received books, magazines, agricultural publications, and military periodicals.
subfiles.summary: Book and periodical review column covering Souza's Impressoes do Japao, Gayda's Que quiere Italia?, an Argentine military review and other works.

subfiles.title: Osaka Syosen Kaisya passenger-service advertisement
subfiles.about: A shipping advertisement offers cabin and third-class passage between Buenos Aires and Japan via Atlantic, Caribbean, Panama, and Pacific ports.
subfiles.summary: Osaka Syosen Kaisya advertisement for a route from Rio Grande to Balboa, Los Angeles, Yokohama and Kobe, with Buenos Aires Maru and Toa Maru departures.

subfiles.title: Oriente y Occidente subscription form
subfiles.about: A detachable form invites subscriptions and submissions to Oriente y Occidente.
subfiles.summary: Oriente y Occidente subscription form with six-month and one-year prices and fields for name and address.

subfiles.title: Opiniones Autorizadas
subfiles.from: Luis Floren; LV2 Radio Central de Córdoba
subfiles.about: A university librarian and a Córdoba radio station praise the magazine and its cultural coverage.
subfiles.summary: Testimonials: Luis Floren asks that the University of Santo Domingo Library receive Oriente y Occidente, and a Cordoba radio station review praises its style and contributors.

subfiles.title: Despatch concerning Leon Siguenza, Salvadoran Consul General at Tokyo
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: The Embassy reports the results of inquiries into Leon Siguenza, his recall by El Salvador, and his background and reputation in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Despatch: El Salvador accepted Consul General Leon Siguenza's resignation effective May 6, 1941; he sought a U.S. visa to leave around August 21, and he had fourteen years in Tokyo and a poor reputation.

subfiles.title: Letter of transmittal
subfiles.from: Sherman Miles, Acting Assistant Chief of Staff, G-2
subfiles.to: A. A. Berle Jr., Department of State
subfiles.about: Military Intelligence forwards seven communications to the State Department for information and possible action.
subfiles.summary: Brigadier General Sherman Miles sends A. A. Berle Jr. enclosures on America First speakers, alleged Nazi agents, film-can communication with South America, and other matters.

subfiles.title: Axis Communication with South America by Means of Film Cans
subfiles.doc_type: Military Intelligence Division summary of information
subfiles.to: G-2; War Department Censorship Branch; Panama Canal Department; DIO, 34th Naval District, New York; O.A.
subfiles.about: A military intelligence summary reports an alleged secret messaging system between South America and Japan using motion-picture film cans.
subfiles.summary: MID summary: a reliable source says messages are hidden in motion-picture film cans shipped from South American cities to Japan, where intelligence agents retrieve them; evaluated as credible.
